title: Xbox is officially embracing the chaos of AI-powered game ports
key_facts: Microsoft has created a new Xbox Labs group to experiment with decompiling and recompiling games.
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma describes it as a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things players and developers can experience.

It follows recent fan projects that decompiled and rebuilt games to run on hardware they were not designed for, such as Windows builds on Apple Silicon and games running in a web browser; many of them use AI models, according to The Verge.
Sharma says Xbox will "build in the open" and share the tools it makes with developers across the industry.
Sharma says people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing Xbox games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide.

The Verge's view: the bigger question is how Microsoft will respond when modders make its game code freely available; Microsoft did not respond in time to a request for comment on unauthorized use of its intellectual property.
quote_evidence: Microsoft has created a new Xbox Labs group to experiment with decompiling and recompiling games.
I asked Microsoft to comment about unauthorized IP use, but the company didn’t respond in time for publication.
We’ll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating.
why_it_matters_hint: Microsoft is officially backing AI-assisted game ports and remixes, while the question of who owns the results is open.
event_date: 13 Oct 2026 (The Verge publication time); exact announcement date not stated in the article
notes: The Verge's commentary (what Microsoft may do about unauthorized copies) is the writer's opinion and is attributed as such. Sharma's statements are quoted in the article, which also reproduces her post.
